bull.b: The sharp revenue recovery and higher gross margin show improved commercial scale and operating economics. If sustained, this combination can strengthen the earnings base, although the historical volatility means durability is not yet proven.

A shift from heavy cash burn to positive operating and free cash flow improves financial self-funding capacity. Even though the cushion remains small, continued conversion would reduce reliance on external capital and support operational resilience.

The latest reported period indicates broad-based improvement across revenue, gross profit, operations, assets, and equity. A wider improvement than revenue alone may provide a more durable foundation for recovery if subsequent periods confirm the trend.

bear.b: Despite the revenue rebound, the company still loses money overall and generates only a thin operating margin. This limits retained capital, increases sensitivity to cost or demand pressure, and leaves the recovery dependent on further execution improvements.

Debt remains slightly above equity and materially constrains financial flexibility, despite improvement from 2025. Elevated leverage can amplify downside during cyclical weakness, restrict investment capacity, and increase dependence on sustained cash generation.

Access to a sizeable equity facility provides funding flexibility but creates potential dilution if shares are issued. It also signals that external capital may remain relevant while profitability and free-cash-flow generation are not yet consistently sufficient.
